🦴 *SPINE TIP OF THE WEEK*

*THE 10-SECOND SCOLIOSIS CHECK*
*Could Your Child Have a Curved Spine?*

Many children with scoliosis have *no pain at all*, which is why it often goes unnoticed until the curve becomes more obvious.

The good news? A simple 10-second check at home can help identify early warning signs.

👀 *What to look for:*
✅ One shoulder higher than the other
✅ Uneven waistline
✅ One side of the rib cage appearing more prominent
✅ Leaning to one side while standing
✅ Uneven posture in photographs

💡 *Try this simple test:*
Ask your child to stand with feet together, bend forward, and touch their toes while you observe from behind.

Early detection can make a significant difference, especially during growth spurts between *10–16 years of age*.

Remember:
👉 Not every uneven shoulder means scoliosis.
👉 But if you notice any of these signs, it's worth getting the spine evaluated.

A quick 10-second check today could make a lifelong difference tomorrow.

Many runners have excellent cardiovascular fitness and endurance, but running alone may not fully protect against age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), reduced strength, or declining bone health.

Benefits of regular strength training for runners:
✅ Improved running efficiency

✅ Reduced injury risk
✅ Stronger muscles and bones
✅ Prevention of age-related muscle loss

Do you spend several hours daily looking at your phone, laptop, or tablet?

Prolonged screen use can place excessive stress on the cervical spine, leading to a condition commonly known as **Text Neck Syndrome**. As the head tilts forward, the load on the neck muscles and cervical discs increases significantly, contributing to neck pain, shoulder stiffness, headaches, poor posture, and upper back discomfort.

A simple habit can help:
✅ Hold your phone closer to eye level
✅ Avoid prolonged neck flexion
✅ Take movement breaks every 20–30 minutes
✅ Perform gentle neck and upper back stretches regularly

Minimally Invasive Spine Surgery (MISS) provides an advanced alternative to traditional open surgery by utilizing smaller incisions to access the spine. This technique aims to treat various spinal conditions while significantly reducing muscle and tissue damage.
Key Benefits of MISS
Faster Recovery: Patients often experience shorter hospital stays and a quicker return to work and daily activities, sometimes within two to three weeks.
Reduced Physical Impact: The smaller entry lead to less blood loss during the procedure and decreased postoperative pain.
Lower Risk: Minimizing the surgical field results in a reduced risk of infection.

Disc Prolapse: Also known as herniated or slipped discs.
Lumbar Stenosis: Narrowing of the spinal canal that puts pressure on nerves.
Spinal Instability: Cases where the vertebral bones or joints need stabilization.
Spondylolisthesis: When one vertebra slips forward over another.

Why Are My Legs Tingling? Understanding Numbness and "Pins and Needles"
​Have you noticed a persistent tingling or numbness in your legs? While it’s often just a limb "falling asleep," recurring sensations can be a signal from your body that something deeper—like a pinched nerve or poor circulation—needs attention.

​Spinal Issues: Conditions like a herniated disc or spinal stenosis often cause radiating leg pain (sciatica).

What I found in him was someone who didn't just treat the condition — he genuinely understood what I was going through.

And that's what truly sets him apart. He has a rare ability to read a patient — not just their charts, but their state of mind. He seems to know instinctively when you need a detailed explanation, when you need reassurance, and when you simply need someone to be steady for you. There's a level-headedness about him that never wavers, whether it's a routine follow-up or a moment of real worry. He doesn't panic, he doesn't rush, and he never makes you feel like your concerns are too small to address.

His calmness is something I can't quite put into words. And that reassurance extends well beyond the clinic. No matter the time or time zone, Dr. Bajwa has always been available. For a patient navigating recovery, that accessibility means more than I can express.

For both my hip replacements, he performed the Direct Anterior Approach — a minimally invasive technique that works with your muscles rather than cutting through them. The recovery felt natural and the restoration of function was remarkable. I came out of it not just pain-free, but genuinely restored — in both body and in mind.

His team, too, is a true reflection of him — warm, attentive, and supportive at every step.

I've been his patient for two years now, and I mean this with complete sincerity — no matter which corner of the world I am in, or he is in, if I ever need a hip surgery/revision surgery again, there is no one else I would go to. That's not loyalty out of habit. That's the kind of trust that can only be earned, and Dr. Bajwa has earned it completely.

I would recommend him without hesitation to anyone facing a hip or joint replacement. You won't just find an exceptional surgeon — you'll find someone who truly cares about giving you your life back.

❓ Patient FAQ Thursday

**My MRI Shows a Disc Bulge. Should I Be Worried?**

One of the most common concerns patients have after an MRI is seeing the words **"disc bulge"** in the report. Fortunately, a disc bulge does **not** automatically mean you have a serious spinal problem or that you need surgery.

A disc bulge is a common MRI finding and is often seen even in people who have no back pain or leg pain. This is why MRI findings should always be interpreted alongside your symptoms and a thorough clinical examination.

Key Things to Know:

✔ A disc bulge is common and may be a part of normal age-related changes.
✔ Many people with disc bulges have no symptoms.
✔ Most patients improve with medications, physiotherapy, activity modification, and guided rehabilitation.
✔ Surgery is required only in selected cases, such as progressive neurological weakness, loss of bladder or bowel control, or persistent disabling pain despite appropriate conservative treatment.

Remember:

**Treat the patient, not just the MRI.**

Your symptoms, physical examination, lifestyle, and functional limitations are far more important than the MRI report alone in deciding the right treatment.

If you've been diagnosed with a disc bulge or slipped disc and are unsure what it means, consult a spine specialist for a comprehensive evaluation and personalized treatment plan.

🩺 **Dr. Siddharth Katkade**
Consultant Spine Surgeon
Bombay Spine Clinic™

⚖️ MYTH vs FACT

❌ Myth: Every Slip Disc Requires Surgery

✅ Fact: Most patients improve without surgery.

A slip disc diagnosis can be worrying, but surgery is not the answer for everyone. In fact, most patients recover successfully with medications, physiotherapy, lifestyle modifications, and guided rehabilitation.

Surgery is generally reserved for selected situations such as persistent severe pain, progressive neurological weakness, or loss of bladder and bowel control.

The most important principle in spine care is to treat the patient's symptoms and clinical condition—not just the MRI report.

If you are experiencing back pain, leg pain, or have concerns about your MRI findings, a proper clinical evaluation can help determine the best treatment approach.

🩺 Dr. Siddharth Katkade
Consultant Spine Surgeon
Bombay Spine Clinic™

🦴 *SPINE TIP OF THE WEEK*

*THE 10-SECOND SCOLIOSIS CHECK*
*Could Your Child Have a Curved Spine?*

Many children with scoliosis have *no pain at all*, which is why it often goes unnoticed until the curve becomes more obvious.

The good news? A simple 10-second check at home can help identify early warning signs.

👀 *What to look for:*
✅ One shoulder higher than the other
✅ Uneven waistline
✅ One side of the rib cage appearing more prominent
✅ Leaning to one side while standing
✅ Uneven posture in photographs

💡 *Try this simple test:*
Ask your child to stand with feet together, bend forward, and touch their toes while you observe from behind.

Early detection can make a significant difference, especially during growth spurts between *10–16 years of age*.

Remember:
👉 Not every uneven shoulder means scoliosis.
👉 But if you notice any of these signs, it's worth getting the spine evaluated.

A quick 10-second check today could make a lifelong difference tomorrow.

📤 Please share this with parents, teachers, coaches, school groups, and anyone involved in children's health and development. Early awareness matters. 😊

🏃‍♂️ Spine Tip of the Week | The Runner's Paradox

Many runners have excellent cardiovascular fitness and endurance, but running alone may not fully protect against age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), reduced strength, or declining bone health.

While running trains your heart, strength training helps protect your muscles, bones, joints, and spine.

Benefits of regular strength training for runners:
✅ Improved running efficiency
✅ Better spine support
✅ Reduced injury risk
✅ Stronger muscles and bones
✅ Prevention of age-related muscle loss

A simple goal: For every 3–4 running sessions per week, include at least 2 strength-training sessions. Even 20 minutes twice weekly can make a meaningful difference.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we encourage runners and active individuals to focus on both endurance and strength for long-term spine health and injury prevention.

📍 Bombay Spine Clinic

Long hours of sitting can put extra stress on your spine, leading to back pain, neck stiffness, and posture problems. Poor sitting habits may also affect spinal discs and reduce flexibility over time.

💡 Healthy Spine Tip:
Take a short break every 30 minutes.

Spinal TB: Treatable without Surgery with Timely Care
Spinal tuberculosis (TB), also known as Pott’s spine is a serious but treatable condition that requires timely diagnosis and appropriate management. If not treated on time, it can lead to severe pain, spinal deformity, and even neurological complications. Dr Bhavin Shial best Spine TB specialist in Mumbai explains that early intervention with anti-tubercular drugs can prevent complications and help patients regain normal mobility without surgery. Minimally Invasive Spine Surgery (MISS) provides an advanced alternative to traditional open surgery by utilizing smaller incisions to access the spine. This technique aims to treat various spinal conditions while significantly reducing muscle and tissue damage.
Key Benefits of MISS
Faster Recovery: Patients often experience shorter hospital stays and a quicker return to work and daily activities, sometimes within two to three weeks.
Reduced Physical Impact: The smaller entry lead to less blood loss during the procedure and decreased postoperative pain.
Lower Risk: Minimizing the surgical field results in a reduced risk of infection.
Aesthetic Results: Smaller incisions lead to minimal scarring compared to traditional methods.

MISS is used for several common spinal issues :- 
Disc Prolapse: Also known as herniated or slipped discs.
Lumbar Stenosis: Narrowing of the spinal canal that puts pressure on nerves.
Spinal Instability: Cases where the vertebral bones or joints need stabilization.
Spondylolisthesis: When one vertebra slips forward over another.
